result: The Drosophila olfactory system serves as a conserved model for studying neural circuit wiring mechanisms. The antennal lobe is functionally equivalent to the vertebrate olfactory bulb, and molecules/mechanisms identified in Drosophila have been shown to play similar roles in mammalian brain wiring.
evaluation: C1 establishes the anatomical equivalence between Drosophila and vertebrate olfactory systems based on established knowledge. C2 is supported by three independent citations demonstrating conservation of wiring mechanisms across species. These claims provide appropriate context for the model system.

result: PN dendritic patterning creates a prototypic olfactory map prior to ORN axon innervation, demonstrating PN-autonomous targeting ability. PNs are derived from anterodorsal and lateral lineages with invariant birth order, but previous studies could only follow development of a single PN type (DL1).
evaluation: Claims C3-C6 are well-supported by multiple prior studies (Jefferis et al., 2001-2004; Marin et al., 2005; Yu et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2012) establishing the developmental timeline and PN-autonomous nature of initial map formation. C7 appropriately identifies the limitation that motivated the current study. These claims establish the foundation and rationale for the work.

result: The adult-specific antennal lobe develops alongside degeneration of the larval-specific antennal lobe during early metamorphosis. The developing antennal lobe grows from 0-12 hr APF as PN dendrites innervate it, with PNs sorting dendrites into specific regions by 12 hr APF to form a prototypic map, followed by gradual segregation into non-overlapping glomeruli by 50 hr APF.
evaluation: Claims C10-C14 are supported by imaging data in Figure 1D1-5 showing the spatial and temporal progression of antennal lobe development. The observations are consistent with prior work (C8-C9 citing Marin et al., 2005) and provide appropriate developmental context. Sample sizes are provided for each timepoint.

result: The authors generated new genetic tools using CRISPR/Cas9 to insert T2A-QF2 immediately before stop codons of endogenous genes (CG14322, lov, tsh), creating knock-in driver lines that express QF2 in the same pattern as endogenous genes. These QF2 lines operate orthogonally to GAL4/UAS systems, enabling simultaneous labeling of distinct PN types.
evaluation: C16-C17 are supported by transcriptomic data (Figure 2A-B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1-2) and molecular biology methods. C18 is supported by citation to Diao and White, 2012. C19 is supported by citations to Potter et al., 2010 and Riabinina et al., 2015. The genetic strategy is well-documented and builds on established methods.

result: DL1 PN dendrites show robust growth by the wandering third instar larval stage, extend radially across the developing antennal lobe at 0 hr APF, concentrate at the dorsolateral corner by 6 hr APF, maintain this position as the antennal lobe grows, and undergo progressive refinement from 21-50 hr APF to form a compact posterior glomerulus.
evaluation: Claims C20-C24 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3A1-6 with appropriate sample sizes (N=4-14 per timepoint). C20 is additionally supported by citation to Jefferis et al., 2004. The temporal progression is well-documented and provides a baseline for comparison with other PN types.

result: Early larval-born adPNs (DL1, DA3, DC2) develop similarly and share targeting to the dorsolateral corner from 0-12 hr APF, with substantial dendritic overlap. Beginning at 21 hr APF, these PNs segregate along medial-lateral and anterior-posterior axes, eventually forming distinct glomeruli separated by intermediate glomeruli by 50 hr APF.
evaluation: Claims C25-C32 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3B1-6 comparing DL1/DA3 and DC2 PN development with appropriate sample sizes (N=2-12 per timepoint). C27 and C33-C34 are reasonable inferences from the temporal progression observed. The data demonstrate that PNs with adjacent birth order initially target similar regions before segregating.

result: Larval-born adPNs with adjacent birth order send dendrites to similar regions while those with distant birth order target distinct regions. The birth order correlates with dendrite targeting in an organized, rotating manner (clockwise in right hemisphere): early→DL; mid-early→VL; mid-late→M/DM; late→pDM.
evaluation: Claims C35-C39 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3C1-4 and Figure 3D1-9 using both genetic drivers and MARCM clones with appropriate sample sizes. C40-C42 are reasonable inferences summarizing the spatial organization pattern. The rotating pattern represents a novel finding about the logic of initial map formation.

result: Larval-born adPN dendrites innervate and pattern the antennal lobe using a 'first born, first developed' strategy. At 0 hr APF, DL1 PN dendrites are more elaborate than mid-late born PNs, but by 6 hr APF mid-late born PNs catch up. Early-born adPNs concentrate dendrites by 6 hr APF while later-born PNs concentrate dendrites by 12 hr APF.
evaluation: C43 is supported by quantitative analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 3F. C44-C46 are supported by imaging data in Figure 3B2, Figure 3D4-9, and supplementary figures with appropriate sample sizes. C47 is a reasonable inference from the temporal progression data. The 'first born, first developed' principle is well-supported.

result: lPN dendrites pattern the developing antennal lobe following similar developmental rules as adPNs (adjacent birth order→similar targeting; distant birth order→distinct targeting; 'first born, first developed'), but with a binary rather than rotating pattern: early→M/DM; middle→VL; late→DM. Lineage and birth order contribute combinatorially to dendrite targeting, represented as [lineage, birth order]=dendrite targeting.
evaluation: Claims C48-C53 are supported by imaging data in Figure 4A1-3, Figure 4B1-6, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3D with appropriate sample sizes. C54-C55 are reasonable inferences from the data. C56 corroborates with prior work (Jefferis et al., 2004). C57-C58 represent the key conceptual framework synthesizing the findings. The combinatorial logic is well-supported by the systematic characterization.

result: An early pupal brain explant culture system recapitulates key features of in vivo olfactory circuit development, including brain morphology changes, dynamic dendritic protrusions followed by extensive innervation, direction-specific axon outgrowth, pruning of larval-specific dendrites, antennal lobe growth, stereotyped dendrite targeting, and segregation of neighboring proto-glomeruli.
evaluation: Claims C59-C69 are supported by multiple lines of evidence: C59 by citation to Rabinovich et al., 2015; C60-C69 by imaging data in Figure 5D-G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 with appropriate sample sizes. The explant system validation is thorough, demonstrating that key developmental events occur ex vivo, albeit at a slower rate (C65). This establishes the foundation for subsequent time-lapse imaging experiments.

result: Two-photon time-lapse imaging of single DL1 PNs reveals that dendrite targeting specificity increases over time through active targeting in specific directions and stepwise elimination of unfavorable trajectories. DL1 PNs progress through initial (exploration in all directions), transitional (~4 hr, predominantly 2 of 4 directions with DL always included but never VM), and final (preference for DL) phases.
evaluation: Claims C70-C76 are supported by two-photon imaging data in Figure 6A-G with quantitative analysis of dendritic volume in different directions over time (N=3 samples). C77 is a reasonable inference summarizing the mechanism. The stepwise elimination process and directional selectivity are clearly demonstrated, though the sample size is modest (N=3).

result: AO-LLSM imaging reveals that PNs achieve dendrite targeting specificity through direction-dependent branch stabilization on the timescale of seconds. At 3 hr APF, DL1 PNs constantly produce, eliminate, extend, and retract branches at ~1.5 μm/min, with significantly fewer stable branches in the VM direction. By 12 hr APF, direction-specific de/stabilization ceases, stable branch abundance peaks, branch speed decreases to ~1 μm/min, and dendritic arborization increases.
evaluation: Claims C78-C85 are supported by AO-LLSM imaging data in Figure 7A-E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1 with quantitative analysis of branch dynamics (N=3-4 samples per timepoint). Statistical significance is shown for key comparisons (C80, C84). C86-C87 are reasonable inferences from the data. The high temporal resolution (30 sec intervals) provides unprecedented insight into branch dynamics, though sample sizes are modest.

result: Embryonic-born PNs re-extend adult-specific dendrites as early as 3 hr APF, before larval-specific dendrites are completely pruned. By 6 hr APF, lov+ PNs show extensive dendritic innervation, and by 12 hr APF they have caught up with larval-born DC2 PNs in development. Re-extension occurs dorsal to larval-specific dendrites, and fragmentation occurs at distal ends rather than by proximal severing.
evaluation: Claims C88-C98 are supported by imaging data in Figure 8A-D and Figure 8—figure supplement 2-3 with appropriate sample sizes (N=3-12 per timepoint). C88 cites prior work (Marin et al., 2005). C90, C93, C95, and C98 are reasonable inferences from the observations. The data demonstrate simultaneous pruning and re-extension at spatially distinct locations, representing a novel remodeling mechanism.

result: Both dendritic pruning and re-extension of embryonic-born PNs require ecdysone signaling in a cell-autonomous manner. Inhibition of ecdysone signaling by EcR-DN expression suppresses both processes. Simultaneous pruning and re-extension at spatially distinct regions explains how embryonic-born PNs can timely re-integrate into the adult olfactory circuit and engage in prototypic map formation.
evaluation: C99 is supported by citation to Marin et al., 2005. C100 is supported by experimental data in Figure 8—figure supplement 4 showing that EcR-DN blocks both pruning and re-extension (N≥3 per stage per genotype). C101-C102 are reasonable inferences from the combined observations. The dual requirement for ecdysone signaling in both processes is clearly demonstrated, though the authors note they cannot distinguish whether re-extension failure is secondary to pruning defects.

result: PNs use lineage and birth order combinatorially to build the initial dendritic map, with birth order directing dendrite targeting in rotating and binary manners for anterodorsal and lateral lineages, respectively. PN dendrites initiate active targeting with direction-dependent branch stabilization on the timescale of seconds. PNs used in both larval and adult circuits prune and re-extend dendrites simultaneously to facilitate timely map organization.
evaluation: These abstract claims (C103-C106) are high-level summaries of the major findings supported by the detailed results described in previous claim groups. C103-C104 summarize the wiring logic findings (supported by claims C40-C42, C54-C58). C105 summarizes the cellular mechanism findings (supported by claims C77, C86-C87). C106 summarizes the remodeling findings (supported by claims C93-C95, C101-C102). All are well-supported by the data presented.
